facts.fact_text: The applicant intended to organise demonstrations in order to call attention to the situation of those having sustained damage originating in a major bankruptcy case which had attracted considerable media attention in Hungary.
On 5 February 2007 the applicant applied to the Budapest Police Department for acquiescence in a demonstration on 10 March 2007 scheduled in Kossuth Square, in front of Parliament.

On 5 February 2007 the applicant applied to the Budapest Police Department for acquiescence in a demonstration of ongoing nature, from 10 March until 31 October 2007, scheduled in Kossuth Square, in front of Parliament.

On 5 February 2007 the applicant applied to the Budapest Police Department for acquiescence in a demonstration of ongoing nature, from 10 March until 31 October 2007, scheduled in Kossuth Square, in front of Parliament.
On 7 February 2007 the Budapest Police Department refused to deal with the applicant's application for acquiescence in a demonstration on 10 March 2007.
On 7 February 2007 the Budapest Police Department refused to deal with the applicant's application for acquiescence in an ongoing demonstration from 10 March until 31 October 2007.

On 23 October 2006 the Budapest Police Department declared the area of Kossuth Square, in front of Parliament, a "security operational zone" (biztonsági műveleti terület) in view of the tumultuous events in Budapest in September 2006.
The "security operational zone" declaration was, after a prolongation, in place for an indefinite period of time.

The Budapest Police Department observed that the "security operational zone" measure remained outside the Budapest Police Department's competence as regards the prohibition of, or acquiescence in, a demonstration.
On 5 March 2007 the National Police Commander upheld the Budapest Police Department's decision of 7 February 2007 refusing to deal with the applicant's applications.
On 14 January 2008 the Budapest Regional Court dismissed the applicant's request for judicial review of the police authorities' decisions.
The Budapest Regional Court's dismissal of the applicant's request for judicial review endorsed in essence the police authorities' reasoning.

On 29 January 2007 a Mr K. challenged the Budapest Police Department's decision to declare Kossuth Square a "security operational zone".
On 14 March 2007 the Budapest Police Commander rejected Mr K.'s complaint challenging the declaration of Kossuth Square as a "security operational zone".
The Budapest Police Commander's decision of 14 March 2007 rejecting Mr K.'s complaint was quashed by the National Police Commander on 16 April 2007.

In the resumed administrative proceedings, on 22 June 2007 the Budapest Police Commander again rejected Mr K.'s complaint challenging the declaration of Kossuth Square as a "security operational zone".
On 19 July 2007 the National Police Commander upheld the Budapest Police Commander's decision of 22 June 2007 rejecting Mr K.'s complaint.
Mr K. challenged the National Police Commander's ruling of 19 July 2007 in court.
Mr K.'s court action challenging the National Police Commander's ruling of 19 July 2007 was dismissed by the Budapest Regional Court.
On appeal, the Supreme Court quashed the Budapest Regional Court's decision dismissing Mr K.'s action.
On appeal, the Supreme Court quashed the National Police Commander's decision of 19 July 2007.
In the resumed second-instance administrative proceedings, on 23 December 2009 the National Police Commander again upheld the Budapest Police Commander's decision rejecting Mr K.'s complaint.
Mr K. requested judicial review of the National Police Commander's decision of 23 December 2009.

On 11 November 2010 the Budapest Regional Court, in judgment no. 27.K.31.354/2010/9., quashed both the first-instance and the second-instance administrative decisions concerning Mr K.'s complaint about the "security operational zone" in Kossuth Square.
On 11 November 2010 the Budapest Regional Court, in judgment no. 27.K.31.354/2010/9., remitted the case to the Budapest Police Commander.

The Budapest Regional Court pointed out in judgment no. 27.K.31.354/2010/9. that the impugned administrative decisions did not contain any concrete elements establishing the necessity and proportionality of maintaining the "security operational zone" after the prolongation of 22 November 2006.

The Budapest Regional Court pointed out in judgment no. 27.K.31.354/2010/9. that the impugned administrative decisions did not address Mr K.'s suggestion that the mere fencing-off of Parliament's immediate vicinity — rather than the global ban on Kossuth Square — would have been sufficient in the circumstances.
In the resumed first-instance administrative proceedings, on 4 April 2011 the Budapest Police Commander partly sustained Mr K.'s complaint.

The Budapest Police Commander, in partly sustaining Mr K.'s complaint on 4 April 2011, noted that, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, the proportionality of the "security operational zone" measure had successfully been challenged.
